blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Department of Official Language (DoOL) oversees official language implementation.
Committee of Parliament on Official Language (CPOL) monitors official language usage across India.
Rajbhasha Vibhag constitutes the ministry and implementation structure for language policy.
Central Hindi Training Institute (CHTI) focuses on language training and skill development.
Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee) functions as an apex policy-making body.

cells: Under Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA); headed by a Secretary

Frame and implement Official Language Policy; issue Annual Programme; coordinate with all Ministries and PSUs; inspect offices for compliance; conduct training through CHTI; issue guidelines on Hindi in computers
Annual targets for use of Hindi in correspondence, noting, original drafting; issued to all Central Govt offices; quarterly progress reviewed
DoOL teams inspect Central Govt offices periodically; check compliance with OL Rules 1976; give recommendations; Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskaar given to best performing offices

blocks.content: 8.2 Committee of Parliament on Official Language (CPOL)

cells: Constituted under Section 4 of Official Languages Act 1963; 30 members (20 Lok Sabha + 10 Rajya Sabha)

Review progress made in use of Hindi for official purposes of the Union; submit report to President; President places report before both Houses of Parliament with his comments; recommendations forwarded to all States
Has submitted 9 reports so far; recommendations guide Hindi policy; last report is being implemented; covers bank Hindi implementation, education, courts, All India Radio, etc.
Has sub-committees touring various states and Central Government offices; assess Hindi use; interact with local officials
Policy; Annual Programme; inspection; training; awards; Hindi in computers
Implement OL policy in ministry; coordinate Hindi training; send QPR; conduct Hindi competitions during Hindi Month
Coordinate among Central Govt offices in a town; share best practices; quarterly meetings; awards to member offices
Rajbhasha Vibhag / Hindi Cell at HO and Circle Offices
Implement RBI/DoOL guidelines; conduct training; prepare QPR; organise Hindi competitions; inspect branches; liaise with TOLIC
Ensure branch compliance; display in Hindi; bilingual forms; Hindi correspondence targets; report to circle office
Central Hindi Training Institute (केन्द्रीय हिन्दी प्रशिक्षण संस्थान)
Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs
New Delhi (HQ); 10 Regional Training Institutes across India (Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Guwahati, Chandigarh, Patna, Ahmedabad, Bhopal, Bengaluru)
Prabodh (Basic), Praveen (Intermediate), Pragya (Advanced), Hindi Typing, Hindi Stenography, Correspondence Course in Hindi
Central Government employees; employees of public sector banks and PSUs; train-the-trainer programmes also available
Prabodh, Praveen, Pragya also available as distance learning courses; employees in remote areas can benefit

items: Focus on the exact duties and administrative hierarchy of the Department of Official Language (DoOL).
Differentiate between the parliamentary role of CPOL and the advisory role of Kendriya Hindi Samiti.
Identify the specific training mandates assigned to the Central Hindi Training Institute (CHTI).

cells: Highest policy-making body for promotion of Hindi; members include senior Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of major states, experts in Hindi and other Indian languages
Review progress in propagation of Hindi; give policy directions; coordinate between states and Centre; meet periodically
Highest level body; its decisions shape Hindi promotion policy across the country
